implementation_limits_recorded.GenerateOrderIdWithTenantId: order_id.go:53-74: 14-digit timestamp at second granularity (the comment claiming milliseconds is wrong), tenant folded to five bytes by tenantPart[:5] or left-padded with '0' via %-5s, then rand.Int32N(10000) printed with %04d. Tenants '12345' and '123456789' therefore share a prefix, and the space per second per tenant is 10^4 while the test draws 1000 ids and demands zero collisions. Not fixable by lowering load or retrying: expected colliding pairs for 1000 draws is about 50.
implementation_limits_recorded.idCounter.Increase: order_id.go:15-20: cur := *c is a plain non-atomic read of shared state, then atomic.AddUint32, then CompareAndSwapUint32(c, 1000, 0) which resets only at exactly 1000, and the stale cur is returned. Concurrent callers can obtain the same index, and the counter only yields 1000 distinct values per second, so the thread test's 1000-distinct-ids-in-one-second assertion cannot be relied on.
implementation_limits_recorded.GenerateOrderIdWithRandom: order_id.go:36 prints the random part with %d rather than %04d, so any value below 1000 shortens the id while order_id_test.go asserts len(prefix)+14+4. Theory says this happens 10% of the time.
